title: Resume is the normal boot path, not the error path
description:
Cloudflare containers are killed at arbitrary moments - 'not guaranteed to run indefinitely... including during host server restarts, which occur on an unpredictable schedule' - and restart with a FRESH DISK. The clone and any unpushed commits are gone, not corrupted.

So every boot must be the same path: fetch, read the run's state from the branch, continue from there. Including the FIRST boot, where it is a no-op. If resume is a separate, rarely-exercised code path it will be broken on the day it is needed.

This is axiom 1 - cold reconstruction from git must always work - and the local reconciler already satisfies it: it re-derives the world each pass, adopts in-flight attempts BY IDENTITY from the attempt marker, and go6 made it continue across resumable stops without a person. The work here is to prove it holds when the DISK is what was lost, not just the process.

The test that matters is destructive: run an epic, kill the container mid-tick, boot a replacement, and show it continues rather than restarting the tick.
